title: Intake Velocity Ledger and Release Buffering for Strategic Accounts
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem statement: Strategic (top) accounts frequently submit high-impact roadmap requests during open intake windows. PMs have difficulty committing to specific sprint or release windows because acceptance has historically been based on ad-hoc triage, which leads to scope slippage, missed expectations, and misaligned engineering allocations. We need a predictable, measurable intake mechanism that protects release commitments while providing a transparent path for escalations and urgent asks.

Proposal summary: Introduce an 'Intake Velocity Ledger' — a ledger-style allocation and burn-rate model that tracks committed scope units for top accounts across a rolling N-cycle horizon. Pair the ledger with a 'Release Buffering' policy: a reserved capacity percentage that is kept unallocated until X days before release to accommodate priority escalations without derailing planned work. The feature includes: (1) intake scoring (velocity units), (2) ledger view in Console for PMs and Solutions Eng, (3) automated buffer reconciliation during sprint planning, and (4) escalation flow with defined SLAs and fallback compensations.

Why this is different: Existing intake artifacts are point-in-time prioritization matrices and high-touch ad-hoc lanes. The ledger formalizes tempo (velocity) over time and gives engineering predictable allocation signals. Release buffering prevents overcommitment while offering a clear, auditable path for exceptions.

Key trade-offs considered: 
- Strict buffering reduces immediate throughput for product releases (cost: slower feature delivery), but increases predictability and reduces hotfix/rollback risk.
- Ledger complexity may add overhead to PM process; we mitigate via automation (auto-scoring, suggested buffer sizes) and a lightweight UI.
- Escalation windows may create perceived unfairness; outcome governance (approval tiers + compensating credits) included.

Operational metrics to track: average intake velocity per account (units/week), buffer utilization rate (% of reserved capacity used pre-release), percentage of releases with emergency backfills, SLA compliance for intake acknowledgment (target: 3 business days), and downstream impact on velocity variance (target: reduce post-release scope churn by 30%).

Acceptance criteria and artifacts: see acceptance_criteria below. Links to initial artifacts: planning doc, scoring spreadsheet, and mockups are listed in links.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger model defined and documented: units, decay window, and mapping to story points/effort
Console wireframe shows ledger per-customer with current balance, 3-cycle projection, and buffer slider
Auto-scoring prototype implemented as a backend job (PoC) that converts intake forms to velocity units
Buffering policy integrated into release planning checklist and enforced as an advisory constraint in Console
Escalation flow defined with approval tiers and fallbacks; runbook published
Pilot with 3 strategic accounts completed and post-pilot retrospective with metrics collected

2025-02-16 - Emily Park (Design): Shared low-fidelity wireframes for ledger card and buffer slider. Suggests inline help for 'velocity unit' mapping to story points.

2025-02-18 - Rahul Singh (Engineering): Flagged potential data consistency issue when ledger and sprint plan are edited concurrently. Proposed optimistic locking and reconciliation job. Tagged ENG-3002 as dependency.

2025-02-20 - Liam O'Connor: Approved moving to 'Planned'. Next: define pilot success metrics and schedule design handoff for Console mockups.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Week 1-2): Design finalization and alignment with Release Management
Phase 1 (Week 3-6): Backend PoC for auto-scoring + ledger data model (ENG-3002) and Console mockups
Phase 2 (Week 7-10): Pilot with 3 strategic accounts; monitor metrics and collect qualitative feedback
Phase 3 (Week 11-12): Policy adjustments, GA enablement for all enterprise accounts, and playbook publication
decision_log: 2025-02-15: Chosen ledger unit = 'velocity unit' mapped to 1 unit = ~2 engineering story points (approx.), decided to allow PM adjustment per-item
2025-02-17: Default buffer set to 12% of release capacity with configurable slider (range 5%-20%); approved by Release Manager
2025-02-19: Escalation approval tiers set: Solutions Eng review for <= 10 units, Director approval for 11-30 units, VP approval for >30 units
